static_findings.snippet: | `width` | Number | Custom output width in pixels |
| `height` | Number | Custom output height in pixels |
| `useProxy` | String\|Boolean | Enable CORS proxy (URL or true for default) |
| `exclude` | String | CSS selector for elements to hide |
1. **Performance**: Use `scale` instead of `width`/`height` for better performance
2. **Fonts**: Set `embedFonts: true` to ensure custom fonts appear correctly
3. **CORS Issues**: Use `useProxy: true` if images fail to load
5. **Quality**: For PNG/JPG, use `quality: 0.95` for best quality
- Try `straighten: false` if transforms are causing issues
- **Orbit CSS Toolkit** - Companion toolkit by Zumerlab (https://github.com/zumerlab/orbit)

content.value_statement: Teams often need reliable images of styled HTML without rebuilding layouts by hand. This skill guides snapDOM setup, capture options, exports, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Explains npm, yarn, CDN module, and UMD setup paths.
Shows reusable and one-step capture flows for DOM elements.
Covers SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, and Blob exports.
Documents options for scale, dimensions, fonts, exclusions, shadows, and transforms.
Describes CORS proxy fallback, plugin hooks, and performance tuning.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not include executable helper scripts.
Browser behavior, CORS rules, and loaded fonts can affect output.
External proxies should be trusted before capturing protected content.
It does not replace full browser screenshot tools for whole-page automation.

use_cases.title: Export UI Components
use_cases.description: Capture styled components for release notes, design reviews, or shareable product assets.

use_cases.title: Create Design Assets
use_cases.description: Turn live HTML cards, charts, and banners into image assets without rebuilding them manually.

use_cases.title: Prepare Documentation Images
use_cases.description: Generate consistent screenshots for tutorials, launch notes, and component documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to capture a single HTML element with snapDOM and export it as a PNG. Include setup and common options.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Social Preview
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me export a card element at 1200 by 630 pixels with embedded fonts and excluded controls.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Export Formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a snapDOM workflow that exports SVG, PNG, and WebP from one capture result. Explain when to use each format.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Plugin Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a snapDOM plugin approach for a custom exporter. Include lifecycle hooks and safety checks for CORS and fonts.

output_examples.input: Capture a styled dashboard tile for release notes.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the target selector, waits for styles and fonts, chooses PNG output, and recommends a 2x scale.

output_examples.input: Export a chart card as an SVG and a WebP.
output_examples.output: The response recommends reusable capture, explains format tradeoffs, and notes when raster output is better for sharing.
The response checks same-origin access, proxy settings, browser console errors, and safer alternatives for protected assets.

best_practices: Wait for fonts, images, and layout changes before capture.
Use SVG for scalable graphics and PNG or WebP for raster sharing.
Exclude controls, secrets, and transient UI before exporting.
anti_patterns: Do not capture pages that display private user data without consent.
Do not route protected assets through an untrusted CORS proxy.
Do not increase scale on very large elements without testing memory use.

faq.question: Does this skill install snapDOM for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains install options and usage patterns. You choose the package source and run commands yourself.

faq.question: Can it capture pseudo-elements and shadows?
faq.answer: Yes. The source documentation states support for pseudo-elements, shadows, transforms, and Shadow DOM content.

faq.question: Which export formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, Canvas, and Blob outputs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code support.

faq.question: Does it upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The skill describes local captures and downloads, not uploads.

faq.question: What should I check when output is wrong?
faq.answer: Check element size, loaded CSS, loaded fonts, transforms, CORS resources, and output scale.
